why: Semantic paraphrase with no lexical overlap. Catching this needs a classifier, not a pattern -- and R10.11 is explicit that optimized triggers survive perplexity examination, so a classifier moves the boundary rather than closing it.

Cyrillic o (U+043E) for Latin o. This is R10.8's named-but-unimplemented homoglyph clause: it needs a UTS #39 confusables table, and a rule flagging mixed script would fire on most multilingual content the Forum should welcome.
Markdown emphasis splits words. Stripping markup before detection is defensible and not yet done; it would also need the offsets mapped back to the original, since R10.27 reports location.

why: The prefix is present but the key is split below the length threshold. Lowering the threshold to catch fragments would fire on ordinary identifiers; R10.26 makes every credential hit a hard rejection, so that trade is the wrong way round.
A base64-wrapped credential, 60 characters -- under the 120-character encoded-block gate. Decoding candidate base64 and rescanning is the real fix and is bounded work; not yet done.
